thread:
incident-bot: PAGE: detected sustained p99 tail spike in router-usw2 for streaming edges (>2.5s). Alerts: p95=420ms, p99=2.8s, streaming stalls increasing request timeouts. Auto-escalation -> incidents channel.
Maya: seeing the same in the dashboards, started ~12:03UTC. Spike correlates with a routing policy rollout (weighting v2) that started at 11:58UTC.
Rob: confirmed, heatmap shows hot shard groups in us-west-2, traffic skewed to a small set of backend pools. Logs show increased reroutes + backpressure.
Carla: are customers timing out or just delayed? any 5xxs?
Maya: a handful of streaming timeouts (504) for some long-poll connections; most are elevated tail latency but still successful. Two enterprise customers reported partial streaming stalls.
Amber (oncall): I'm oncall-bridge, grabbing ownership. Livebridge up?
ops-bot: livebridge created -> link: https://redwood.incidents/bridge/1832000456
Amber (oncall): Thanks. Rob/Maya, can we confirm root cause: is this a backend overload or router misrouting?
Rob: preliminary: mismatch between new hashing policy and sticky affinity -> hot partitions. Router is sending too much fanout to few shards. Also noticed a misapplied region-weight override for usw2 that increased local affinity.
Levi: I can check router logs and routing-table snapshots. Pulling last commit from rollout: routing-policy:v2 -> diff shows change to consistent-hash seed + prefer-local flag.
Maya: timeline: 11:58 rollout start -> 12:00 weight shift -> 12:03 p99 spike. Fits.
Rob: mitigation idea #1: immediate rollback of routing-policy to v1 for us-west-2. Mitigation #2: temporary reweighting to smooth distribution. Which is faster?
Amber (oncall): rollback is fast if we flip the feature flag. Rob, can you perform rollback? If not, do reweighting.
Rob: I can roll back. Rolling back routing-policy:v2 -> v1 for region=us-west-2 now.
ops-bot: deploybot: rollback started by Rob at 12:07:05UTC.
Carla: do we need to drain affected routers or will the rollback take effect gracefully?
Rob: rollback updates route table; new connections will see v1. Existing sticky sessions may still route to hot shards for a few minutes. We'll also push a short TTL eviction on sticky cache to accelerate rebalancing.
Rob: issuing command to set sticky-ttl=30s for routers in usw2: 
```
# curl to control plane
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TOKEN' https://control.redwood/api/v1/routers/usw2/override -d '{"sticky_ttl":30}'
```
Maya: running heatmap refresh and KV cache eviction now.
ops-bot: action: sticky-ttl override applied by Rob (12:08:12UTC).
Levi: routing-table diff after rollback shows re-distribution starting, but some hot shards still draining. Fanout for keys K1,K2,K3 is still concentrated. Investigating whether a shard eviction is needed.
Amber (oncall): customer impact note: two enterprise customers (AcmeCorp, BrightPublish) experienced streaming stalls and partial timeouts for ~5-7 minutes. Customer SLO alerted. Need outreach after mitigation.
Carla: can we temporarily route those customers to alternate region (e.g., eu-west-1) as a mitigation? Risky for data locality but reduces impact.
Rob: I can create a per-customer policy override to steer to euw1 for those two accounts. Doing it now for AcmeCorp.
ops-bot: policy-override applied for customer=AcmeCorp at 12:10:03UTC.
Maya: p99 dropping: 2.8s -> 1.1s within 90s of rollback/TTL change. Streaming stalls reduced.
Levi: still seeing intermittent spikes from sticky cache hits; will force eviction on affected routers as final step.
Rob: forcing graceful router restart on 3 nodes in the hot pool to flush KV cache (staggered). Command running.
ops-bot: restart jobs queued for routers r-usw2-11/12/13.
Amber (oncall): good. I'll update customers and set incident severity to Sev2 -> "partial degradation, paging resolved".
Carla: any permanent follow-ups? We should revert prefer-local change and add a rollout safety check. Also add an automated heatmap alert tied to changes in consistent hash seed/flags.
Maya: filed follow-up ticket: ROUTER-1248 "prevent prefer-local + seed change without gradual canary and heatmap guard".
Levi: I'll backfill telemetry to see why the seed change created such concentrated hotkeys and tighten our canary windows.
Rob: post-mitigation: p95=380ms, p99=480ms, streaming error rate back to baseline. Marking as mitigated but keeping bridge open for 30m for observation.
Amber (oncall): thanks everyone. I'll do the customer communication draft and link the ticket. Leaving bridge open. If p99 creeps back up, page SRE immediately. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: incident update logged -> incident-1832000456, severity=Sev2, state=mitigated by rollback + ttl override.
Maya: adding logs & timeline to the incident page.
Rob: note for postmortem: consider rate-limit for per-key fanout and automatic regional fallback when weight skew > 3x.
Carla: thanks, closing action items for now.
Amber (oncall): handing over to postmortem owners. Bridge will auto-close at 12:37UTC if stable.
ops-bot: bridge closed at 12:37:05UTC (no regressions observed).
